See also: Violeta, violetā, and violetă

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From viola +‎ -eta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [bi.uˈlɛ.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [vi.oˈlə.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [vi.oˈle.ta]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

violeta f (plural violetes)

  1. violet
    Synonym: viola

Derived terms

[edit]
  • violeta africana
  • violeta de penyal
  • violeta roquera

Adjective

[edit]

violeta (invariable)

  1. violet
    Synonym: violat

Further reading

[edit]
  • “violeta”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

Latvian

[edit]

Adjective

[edit]

violeta

  1. inflection of violets:
    1. genitive masculine singular
    2. nominative feminine singular

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
violeta
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

From viola +‎ -eta (diminutive suffix).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /vi.oˈle.tɐ/ [vɪ.oˈle.tɐ], (faster pronunciation) /vjoˈle.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /vi.oˈle.tɐ/ [vɪ.oˈle.tɐ], (faster pronunciation) /vjoˈle.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /vi.oˈle.ta/ [vɪ.oˈle.ta], (faster pronunciation) /vjoˈle.ta/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /vjuˈle.tɐ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /vjuˈle.tɐ/
    • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /bjuˈle.tɐ/

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Hyphenation: vi‧o‧le‧ta

Adjective

[edit]

violeta m or f (plural violetas)

  1. violet

Noun

[edit]

violeta f (plural violetas)

  1. violet (color)
  2. violet (plant)
  3. (Brazil) viola (musical instrument of the violin family)
